note: Literature confirms KDM2B neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM 621474) involves loss-of-function and domain-specific missense variants (notably CxxC zinc finger and JmjC domains) with variable expressivity and functional episignature validation.

evidence.text: In a comprehensive assessment of KDM2B-associated neurodevelopmental disorder, authors evaluated 47 individuals with pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants, finding variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance for loss-of-function variants and JmjC domain variants, alongside distinct CxxC domain variants.

source.title: Comprehensive Assessment of the KDM2B‐Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorder and the 12q24. 31 Microdeletion Syndrome
source.quote: In contrast, our findings point to variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance of loss-of-function variants and JmjC domain variants complicating variant classification and genetic counseling.

numbers.metric: classified pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants

evidence.text: Van Jaarsveld et al. delineated KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and identified the CxxC zinc-finger domain as a mutational hotspot, demonstrating that both loss-of-function and CxxC-domain missense variants cause the disorder and yield specific functional epigenetic signatures.

source.title: Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and its associated DNA methylation signature
source.quote: Both loss-of-function and CxxC-domain missense variants present with a specific subepisignature.
